name: Public Policy (Min)

rules.name: Requirements Overview
rules.desc:
Students who pursue the minor are required to take the courses listed below. Because University rules prohibit double-counting non-introductory courses, the requirements for a minor differ according to the student's major requirements. All students must take, without double counting, at least six courses for five units each toward the minor for a total of 30 units. It is required that students review their course plans with a program administrator. Note: Students are permitted to double-count ECON 1 Principles of Economics. Students with a Major in Economics will not take PUBLPOL50 and must make up the units with another course.
Public Policy students are never required to take a course that duplicates material they have already mastered. Students may, by petition, substitute a different course for a requirement whose material would be duplicative. This flexibility does not reduce the number of units required for the minor.
rules.notes: At most, 10 units of course work may be taken as credit/no credit. Between ECON 102A and ECON 102B, no more than 5 units can be taken for credit/no credit.

rules.name: Elective Courses
rules.desc: Select one or more of the following depending on major requirements.

rules.name: Course plan reviewed with a program administrator

transferPolicy:
Transfer work can be used to satisfy a department’s major requirement. Students should review the University transfer credit process and obtain transfer credit approval by the Public Policy program for specific minor requirements by following the steps below. Please note, Directed Reading and Oxford tutorial course units may only be applied towards Public Policy subplans within the major and may therefore not be applied to a Public Policy minor.

• Complete a Public Policy Program Course Petition Form for each course and attach all necessary documentation (syllabus, completed coursework, a brief statement, and unofficial transcript).

• Submit the above documents to the Undergraduate Student Services Specialist (kronk@stanford.edu)

• Ask the Undergraduate Student Services Specialist (kronk@stanford.edu) to send a copy of the specific course approval paperwork signed by the Public Policy Program Director.

• If your transfer work is approved and once the class is completed, submit your official transcript and the "Transfer Credit Request: Program Elective eForm" to the Registrar’s Office.
reviewNotes: You take ECON 1, ECON 102A, ECON 102B, PUBLPOL 104, PUBLPOL 50 or ECON 50, and one or more electives from the list, at least six courses of five units each and 30 units in all. At most 10 units may be CR/NC, and at most 5 of them in ECON 102A and 102B. Reviewing your course plan with a program administrator is checked by hand, and so are courses you substitute because your major already uses a requirement (an Economics major replaces PUBLPOL 50 with another course).
